findings.claim: The API reference still says that a re-upload over a trashed file at the same path replaces the ghost and gets a new record. After this fix, init answers 409 whenever the trashed file is still on disk, so that sentence describes the behavior the fix removed.
findings.impact: A reader who takes api.md as the contract would believe a same-name upload over a trashed file succeeds, and could re-add the init bypass the fix just removed. Doing so would destroy the trashed copy again. Users are not affected directly.
findings.evidence: docs/reference/api.md:188 (the upload complete row): "a re-upload over a trashed file at that path replaces the ghost and gets a new record." backend/app/services/upload.py:151-152 now raises 409 unconditionally when target_full exists. The only way to reach the ghost purge at upload.py:317-326 is when the trashed row's file is gone from disk, which backend/tests/test_inbox_arrival.py::test_trashed_ghost_is_replaced_and_gets_a_new_row now sets up with an explicit unlink.
findings.repro: Read api.md:188, then upload.py:151-152 and the new test test_upload_over_a_trashed_file_still_on_disk_is_refused, which asserts 409 for this exact case.

bucket_proposal.reason: Documentation that no longer matches the code and invites re-adding the reverted bypass. No declared invariant covers it.

findings.proposed_fix: Delete the clause "and a re-upload over a trashed file at that path replaces the ghost and gets a new record" from docs/reference/api.md:188.

specification_compliance: The fix restores spec §2, 'Upload to a path that already holds a file: 409 at init as today': init_upload (upload.py:151-152) raises 409 unconditionally again, and the router no longer injects db into init (routers/uploads.py:28-44).
upload.py is back within its declared touch points (the session field and the arrival in complete_upload). The stale comment at upload.py:293-296 about init's guarantee is accurate again.

The complete_upload trashed-ghost purge (upload.py:317-326) is unchanged and is pre-existing behavior. It now runs only when the trashed row's on-disk file is already gone, which matches spec step 3, 'deletes the ghost as today'.

The r1 scope findings (F2–F5, SCOPE-2..5: unlisted frontend files FileDetailChrome, ShellLayout, FileDetailShell, MarkdownDocumentLayout, useSelectedFile, ProcessingStageMark/UploadProgress, inboxGrouping, inboxStage, useInboxCount) are not addressed by this fix commit. They remain touch-list gaps.
potential_unspecified_behavior: None introduced by this fix. It only removes the _has_trashed_ghost branch and the db parameter.
regression_risks: None in code found. The fix reverts init_upload to its pre-change body, plus the inbox_source pass-through. The only residual risk is documentary: api.md:188 still advertises the reverted behavior.
test_coverage: test_upload_over_a_trashed_file_still_on_disk_is_refused is parametrized over inbox_source None and 'upload'. It asserts 409, unchanged on-disk content and the row still in Trash, so it would fail if the bypass returned, with or without inbox_source.
test_trashed_ghost_is_replaced_and_gets_a_new_row now unlinks the file before uploading, so it exercises the complete_upload ghost purge and the cascade of the old inbox row on a path init accepts.
No test covers a complete_upload failure after replacing_file over a ghost path. That path is pre-existing and unchanged.

trajectory: One fix round (95d10b9c2). It removes a branch rather than adding one: the _has_trashed_ghost check, its db parameter on init_upload and the db dependency on the init route are all deleted, and init returns to an unconditional 409 when the target exists on disk. The ghost test gains a setup step (unlink) so it models a real ghost, and the new parametrized test pins the restored refusal. It adds no new state or prediction, so this is not a sign of the design being patched. The api.md sentence describing the removed behavior was left behind.
